document.title: Marquee: Flash-Sale Ticketing
document.overviewSummary: Marquee (a made-up company) sells 60,000 stadium seats to 1.8 million fans who all arrive at 10:00. A virtual waiting room at the edge admits fans at a rate the origin can handle. Seat Inventory holds seats for 8 minutes while the fan pays, the Payment Orchestrator fails over between two card processors, and a transactional outbox streams every order to Kafka, where ticketing and the promoter's live dashboard read it at their own pace.

nodes.title: Fans
nodes.subtitle: 1.8M at 10:00
nodes.summary: Everyone who wants a ticket to the stadium tour. Most arrive in the same minute, on phones, many on weak mobile signal.

nodes.title: Marquee App
nodes.subtitle: iOS, Android and web
nodes.summary: Shows the live seat map, holds the fan's queue token and receives the tickets. Talks GraphQL to the API and keeps a WebSocket open for seat updates.

nodes.title: Realtime Hub
nodes.subtitle: WebSocket fan-out
nodes.summary: Keeps 1.2M sockets open at the edge and pushes "seat taken" and "seat freed" to every map. Fire and forget: a missed update is fixed by the next one.

nodes.title: Edge CDN + WAF
nodes.subtitle: 40 PoPs, bot rules
nodes.summary: Terminates TLS close to the fan, blocks known bots, and checks the signed queue token. With a valid token the request skips the waiting room.

nodes.title: Virtual Waiting Room
nodes.subtitle: Admits at a safe rate
nodes.summary: Turns a stampede into a line. Admits 2 of every 5 requests per tick, so the origin never sees more than it can sell to; everyone else sees their place in the queue.

nodes.title: Bot & Fraud Check
nodes.subtitle: Score every buyer
nodes.summary: Scores device, behaviour and payment signals. Above 0.8 the request is refused; between 0.4 and 0.8 the fan gets a challenge.

nodes.title: Identity
nodes.subtitle: OIDC sessions
nodes.summary: Signs fans in and verifies the session on every call. One account can hold at most 6 tickets per show.

nodes.title: Load Balancer
nodes.subtitle: Least connections
nodes.summary: Spreads admitted traffic over the gateway pods, sending each new request to the one with the fewest open connections.

nodes.title: API Gateway
nodes.subtitle: GraphQL federation
nodes.summary: One GraphQL endpoint for the app. Checks the session and bot score, then calls the seat, order and cache services over gRPC.

nodes.title: Seat Map Cache
nodes.subtitle: Redis, 1 s TTL
nodes.summary: Answers seat-map reads, which are 30 times more common than holds. A 1-second TTL keeps the map honest; misses load from the ticket database.

nodes.title: Ticket Database
nodes.subtitle: Postgres, single primary
nodes.summary: Seats, holds and orders in one transactional store, with an outbox table that change-data-capture streams to Kafka. Running at 78% of write capacity at peak.
nodes.comment: Single primary. A synchronous standby is planned for Q1 (RISK-12).

nodes.title: Seat Inventory
nodes.subtitle: Holds seats for 8 minutes
nodes.summary: The heart of the on-sale. Finds the best available seats, locks them for 8 minutes while the fan pays, and never sells a seat twice.

nodes.title: Hold API
nodes.subtitle: HoldSeats, Release
nodes.summary: Validates the request: show, quantity, and the 6-ticket limit.

nodes.title: Best-Seat Allocator
nodes.subtitle: Keeps groups together
nodes.summary: Picks adjacent seats in the best section left, sharded by section so two fans never fight over the same row lock.

nodes.title: Seat Locks
nodes.subtitle: Redis, TTL 8 min
nodes.summary: A short-lived lock per seat, so a hold disappears on its own if everything else fails.

nodes.title: Hold Ledger
nodes.subtitle: Who holds what
nodes.summary: The durable record of every hold, read back to rebuild locks after a restart.

nodes.title: Checkout & Orders
nodes.subtitle: Turns a hold into an order
nodes.summary: Charges the card, converts the hold into sold seats and writes the order and its outbox event in one transaction.

nodes.title: Hold Expiry Sweeper
nodes.subtitle: Frees unpaid holds
nodes.summary: Every 30 seconds, releases holds older than 8 minutes so their seats go back on sale.

nodes.title: Payment Orchestrator
nodes.subtitle: Tokens, 3-D Secure, routing
nodes.summary: The only service that touches card data. Tokenises the card, runs 3-D Secure, and routes the charge to a card processor, with a circuit breaker on each.

nodes.title: Payment API
nodes.subtitle: Idempotency keys
nodes.summary: Rejects a retry that would charge twice: the same idempotency key returns the first result.

nodes.title: Card Vault
nodes.subtitle: Tokens, HSM keys
nodes.summary: Swaps the card number for a token. Nothing outside this level ever sees a card number.

nodes.title: 3-D Secure
nodes.subtitle: Bank challenge
nodes.summary: Asks the fan's bank to confirm it is really them, usually without a prompt.

nodes.title: Processor Router
nodes.subtitle: Weighted 90 / 10
nodes.summary: Sends 90% to Processor A and 10% to B, and shifts everything to B when A's breaker opens.

nodes.title: Adapter A
nodes.subtitle: Processor A API
nodes.summary: Talks to Processor A, with a breaker that opens after 20% errors in 10 seconds.

nodes.title: Adapter B
nodes.subtitle: Processor B API
nodes.summary: Talks to Processor B, the fallback.

nodes.title: Card Processor A
nodes.subtitle: Primary acquirer
nodes.summary: Takes 90% of charges. When it slows down or fails, the orchestrator's breaker opens and Processor B takes over.

nodes.title: Card Processor B
nodes.subtitle: Fallback acquirer
nodes.summary: Kept warm with 10% of traffic so it is known to work on the day it is needed.

nodes.title: Pay in 3
nodes.subtitle: Instalments partner
nodes.summary: Planned for the next tour: split the price into three payments. Drawn now so the team can see where it plugs in.

nodes.title: Order Events
nodes.subtitle: Kafka, 12 partitions
nodes.summary: Every confirmed order as an event. Each reader keeps its own place, so ticketing and the live dashboard read the same events at their own pace and can replay.

nodes.title: Ticket Jobs
nodes.subtitle: FIFO per order
nodes.summary: One job per order, in order. Each job goes to exactly one issuer; after 5 failed tries it moves to the dead-letter queue.

nodes.title: Ticket Dead Letters
nodes.subtitle: Jobs that kept failing
nodes.summary: Parked jobs for a human to look at. Each one is a fan who paid and has no ticket yet, so an alert fires on the first message.

nodes.title: Promoter Dashboard
nodes.subtitle: Sales by the second
nodes.summary: The tour promoter watches sales per section, live, from the order stream.

nodes.title: Ticket Issuer
nodes.subtitle: Barcodes, PDF, wallet pass
nodes.summary: Issues each ticket with a rotating barcode that cannot be screenshotted and resold, renders the PDF and wallet pass, and stores them.

nodes.title: Ticket Wallet
nodes.subtitle: Object storage
nodes.summary: PDFs and wallet passes. Fans download them through the CDN with a signed link that expires.

nodes.title: Notifications
nodes.subtitle: Push, email, SMS
nodes.summary: Tells the fan the tickets are ready. Push and email first; SMS only for fans who have no app.

nodes.title: Push & Email
nodes.subtitle: Delivery provider
nodes.summary: A delivery provider that reaches the phone. If it is down, notifications fall back to SMS.

nodes.title: Legacy SMS Gateway
nodes.subtitle: Being retired
nodes.summary: The old SMS box from the previous platform. Still sends to fans without the app; scheduled to be replaced by the provider's SMS API.
nodes.comment: Replace with the provider SMS API (MIG-7) before the summer tour.

edges.label: Instalments (planned)
edges.comment: Not built yet: drawn to agree the contract.

steps.trace: 1.8M fans press Buy in the same minute.

steps.label: EDGE
steps.trace: The nearest of 40 edge locations answers. The WAF drops 38% of requests as bots.

steps.label: NO TOKEN
steps.trace: No queue token yet, so the fan joins the virtual waiting room.

steps.label: ADMITTED
steps.trace: The room lets in 2 of every 5 per tick, so the origin is never asked for more than it can sell. Loop this run: the red packets are fans told to keep waiting (429).

steps.label: SEAT MAP
steps.trace: Most of what admitted fans do is look at the map, and the cache answers 92% of it.

steps.label: MISS
steps.trace: One read in twelve reaches the database.

steps.label: 10:04 · BUY
steps.trace: A fan who already waited in line taps Buy for two seats in block B.

steps.label: TOKEN OK
steps.trace: The edge checks the signed queue token the waiting room gave out. It is valid, so no second wait.

steps.label: SKIP THE LINE
steps.trace: The request goes straight to the load balancer, past the waiting room.

steps.label: GATEWAY
steps.trace: The pod with the fewest open connections takes it.

steps.label: SIGNED IN · HUMAN
steps.trace: Session verified, and the bot score is 0.03: a real person.

steps.label: SEAT MAP
steps.trace: The map comes from the cache. On a miss the section loads from the database.

steps.label: LOAD SECTION
steps.trace: Cache miss: block B is read from the ticket database and cached for a second.

steps.label: HOLD 2 SEATS
steps.trace: Seat Inventory picks B12-14 and B12-15, side by side. Open it (level badge) to see how.

steps.label: LOCKED · 8 MIN
steps.trace: The rows are locked and the hold is written. Nobody else can buy these seats for 8 minutes.

steps.label: GREY ON EVERY MAP
steps.trace: The hub tells 1.2M open maps that two seats just went. The wire is two-way: the app keeps the socket alive.

steps.label: CHECKOUT
steps.trace: The fan pays. The checkout call carries the hold id and a card token, never the card number.

steps.label: AUTHORISE $184
steps.trace: Checkout asks the Payment Orchestrator to charge the card token. Open it (level badge) to see 3-D Secure and the processor router.

steps.label: APPROVED
steps.trace: Processor A approves the charge. At 350 ms this is the slowest hop of the whole purchase.

steps.label: SOLD
steps.trace: The hold becomes two sold seats.

steps.label: ORDER + OUTBOX
steps.trace: The order and an OrderConfirmed outbox row are written in one transaction, so the event can never be lost.

steps.label: CONFIRMED
steps.trace: The fan sees "You're going!". Tickets follow in seconds: play "Tickets Delivered".

steps.label: CDC
steps.trace: Change-data-capture reads the outbox row and publishes OrderConfirmed to Kafka.

steps.label: LIVE SALES
steps.trace: The promoter's dashboard reads the same event, at its own pace.

steps.label: ISSUE JOB
steps.trace: Ticketing reads it too and queues one job for the order.

steps.label: ONE ISSUER
steps.trace: Exactly one of the four issuers takes the job.

steps.label: PDF + PASS
steps.trace: Two tickets with rotating barcodes, rendered as a PDF and a wallet pass, saved to object storage.

steps.label: ISSUED
steps.trace: TicketsIssued goes to Notifications.

steps.label: IN YOUR WALLET
steps.trace: Push and email reach the phone: "Your tickets are ready".

steps.label: SMS (LEGACY)
steps.trace: Fans without the app get an SMS through the old gateway. Review flags it: it is deprecated and still on this path.

steps.label: DOWNLOAD
steps.trace: The app fetches the ticket through the CDN with a signed link that expires in 10 minutes.

steps.label: CHECKOUT
steps.trace: Checkout carries on as normal: the fan does not know anything is wrong.

steps.label: AUTHORISE
steps.trace: The orchestrator tries Processor A first.

steps.label: TIMEOUT · BREAKER OPENS
steps.trace: Processor A is down. After 20% errors in 10 seconds the breaker opens and stops sending it work.

steps.label: PROCESSOR B
steps.trace: Processor A's fallback takes every charge. It was kept warm with 10% of traffic, so it is known to work.

steps.label: SOLD ANYWAY
steps.trace: The order completes. Press X on Processor B too and see what that would cost.

simulations.name: Hold Expires: Seats Back On Sale

steps.label: EVERY 30 S
steps.trace: The sweeper wakes up, as it does every 30 seconds.

steps.label: RELEASE 312 HOLDS
steps.trace: Holds older than 8 minutes that were never paid are released.

steps.label: BACK ON THE MAP
steps.trace: The freed seats turn green on every open map. Someone still in line gets lucky.

steps.label: HOLD
steps.trace: A fan tries to hold seats.

steps.label: NO PRIMARY
steps.trace: The single primary is down. Holds, orders and the outbox all stop: this is the one known single point of failure.

steps.label: MAP STILL SHOWS
steps.trace: The cache keeps answering seat-map reads for a moment, so the app still looks alive.

steps.label: TICKETS STALL
steps.trace: No outbox, no events: ticketing goes quiet. The fix (a synchronous standby) is planned as RISK-12.

nodes.title: Nightly Snapshots
nodes.subtitle: 03:00 UTC
nodes.summary: Takes a full snapshot of the primary every night.

nodes.title: Backup Job
nodes.subtitle: Copies and verifies
nodes.summary: Copies the snapshot to the vault and test-restores it, because a backup nobody restored is a hope, not a backup.
